assets.modifications: Original work. Drawn from the reference photographs in assets/refs/ under the rules in assets/style/art-bible.md; never traced. The @1x suffix pins the source to one scale: it is stripped before the texture key is formed, so the key ottawa-landmark-parliament-hill is unchanged and no level document moves. It is a full-width background the player skates past, not something held close to the camera, and at 2x it cost 17.14 MiB of decoded texture - 36% of the level - to sharpen it.

assets.title: TrueNorth character rig part "tail-beaver" — The guide's paddle tail: a broad flat scaly oval carried out to the wearer's right, leaning down and away on a scaly stub that leaves the body at the hip and tucks behind the leg, so the tail reads as attached rather than as a rock beside the feet. The tail is one of the two features that make a beaver identifiable at phone size, so it is drawn at full weight and never tucked behind the figure where a front-facing character would hide it. Scale is three cross bands - a rhythm, not a texture fill (art bible 1); an inner ring was tried and removed because it made the paddle read as a shell. Drawn from assets/refs/beaver/beaver-paddle-tail.jpg and beaver-ontario-full-body.jpg.
assets.author: TrueNorth contributors
assets.modifications: Original work. Drawn from the reference photographs in assets/refs/beaver/ under the rules in assets/style/art-bible.md and assets/style/guide.md; never traced.

assets.title: TrueNorth character rig part "head-shell-beaver" — The guide's head in fur, drawn over the shared head part so the rig keeps ONE head geometry: same cranium box, same eye line, same width envelope as every human character, in the beaver's pelt. Flat crown, heavy cheeks and small round ears set LOW and well back at the side of the skull - the arrangement in assets/refs/beaver/beaver-head-and-forepaws.jpg. High rounded ears would read as a bear, which is the mistake this shape was redrawn to fix. Cartoon proportions are identical for every character (docs/content-review.md 6), and this part is how an animal companion joins that canon instead of getting its own.
